hint_ladder.title: Orient
hint_ladder.text: Think about the word 'adverse' in everyday situations. Have you ever heard of 'adverse weather conditions' or an 'adverse reaction'? What feeling d...

hint_ladder.title: Rule
hint_ladder.text: Connect 'adverse' to 'adversary'—your enemy. So it always carries a negative, opposing meaning. It's never positive.

hint_ladder.title: Apply
hint_ladder.text: Look at the options: three are positive words (favorable, beneficial, helpful). Only one is negative. Which one?

hint_ladder.title: Nearly Give Away
hint_ladder.text: If something is adverse, it's against you—the opposite of favorable. So the synonym is 'unfavorable'.

A.text: You might have chosen A because 'favorable' sounds positive, but adverse means negative.

B.text: You might have chosen B because 'beneficial' seems good, but adverse is unfavorable.

D.text: You might have chosen D because 'helpful' is positive, but adverse is the opposite.

next_time_rule: Adversary Rule: 'Adverse' ay kalaban, so negative. Pag nagdududa, tanungin: positive o negative? Dapat negative ang synonym.
deconstruct_text:
Pag narinig mo 'adverse' sa balita, tulad ng 'adverse weather' dahil sa bagyo, alam mong masama ang lagay ng panahon. Kapag may adverse reaction sa gamot, ibig sabihin hindi hiyang. So 'adverse' laging negative.

Mental trick: I-link mo 'adverse' sa 'adversary' — ang kalaban mo. Parang sa barangay basketball, kalaban ang kabilang team, lagi silang against sa 'yo. Kaya 'adverse' = unfavorable, pumapalag.

Tingnan ang choices: A, B, at D puro positive — pabor, nakakatulong. Si C lang ang negative. Syempre, pag-negative ang tanong, negative din ang sagot. Kaya sure ball na 'yan.

Kung napili mo ang A, B, o D, nadale ka ng antonym trap. Basta tandaan: 'Adverse' ay 'kalaban', di pabor. Kaya sa exam, hanapin ang negative synonym—'di ka na malilito.
